functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Shares the first extensor compartment of the wrist with abductor pollicis longus -- both are classically involved in De Quervain's tenosynovitis.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

trigger_points.location_description: Not mapped by Travell and Simons; the source document infers a taut EPB band from its close anatomical relation to abductor pollicis longus. [clinical reasoning]
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: A taut EPB band is inferred to produce local pain at the radial styloid and dorsal thumb MCP region; the documented remote referrers to this region are supinator and brachialis. [clinical reasoning -- not a Travell & Simons figure for EPB itself]
trigger_points.notes: Non-myofascial differential: De Quervain's disease, intersection syndrome, thumb MCP or basal-joint arthritis, Wartenberg's syndrome.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons (1999) Trigger Point Manual, 2nd ed., Vol. 1; Donnelly et al. (2019) 3rd ed. -- no distinct EPB figure exists in either edition; pattern is labelled [clinical reasoning] in this atlas's uploaded wrist muscle reference.

clinical.function_biomechanics: Major: Extension of the thumb MCP joint; extension and abduction of the carpometacarpal joint [1, 5]. At the wrist: Weak radial deviation; negligible flexion–extension effect because its line of pull lies close to the wrist's flexion–extension axis [1, 6]. Importance: Its anatomical variability governs the completeness of De Quervain's release and the interpretation of thumb MCP extension after EPL rupture (EPB can still extend the MCP joint) [4].
clinical.adjacent_structures: Bursae / sheaths: 1st compartment sheath, with a separate EPB subcompartment in a large proportion of wrists [48]. Coupled structures: 1st compartment septum, superficial radial nerve, APL, EPL (variable insertion into the hood), thumb MCP joint [1, 48].

trigger_points.referred_pain: Not mapped by Travell and Simons. A taut EPB band produces local pain at the radial styloid and dorsal thumb MCP region; the documented dorsal-thumb referrers are supinator and brachialis [clinical reasoning] [2, 3].

clinical.non_myofascial_differential: De Quervain's disease, intersection syndrome, thumb MCP or basal-joint arthritis, Wartenberg's syndrome.
clinical.notes: De Quervain's disease: the EPB subcompartment is the usual reason for persistent symptoms after injection or release [47, 48]. EPB participates in intersection syndrome with APL [35]. When EPB inserts into the distal phalanx, retropulsion testing for EPL must be interpreted carefully.
clinical.caveat: Referred-pain maps from Travell and Simons are clinical consensus drawings, not experimentally derived; the APL and pronator quadratus maps (Hwang et al.) are experimental hypertonic-saline studies in healthy volunteers. Grade C items (Appendix A rows 23, 44–46, 48): TrP distances, muscle-level arterial detail, the ECRL/ECRB insertional bursa, the grip-strength claim for PL agenesis, and the extrapolated EDM/EPB/EPL referral statements. All are labelled in the text. Referred-pain conventions. "TrP referral" is the essential (dark) zone described by Travell and Simons unless "spillover" is stated. TrP locations in centimetres are approximations read from the Manual's figures and should be confirmed by palpation of the taut band. Quantitative biomechanical values are cadaveric means and vary with forearm rotation and wrist angle.
